items.title: replace_memory_range on a machine sharing its directory: after destroy + sync_stored the O2-guaranteed directory reloads to a spliced state (old range, new registers)
items.component: Emulator core: machine::replace_memory_range with SHARING_ALL/CONFIG loads, destroy, sync_stored, load (src/machine.cpp ~723-764, ~712)
items.role: Sharing/syncing/loading: Honest operator; replace_memory_range: rest of the machine API (off the PRT path; unsure)
items.severity: Medium (preferred: off-path API operation) / Critical (if a production node replaces ranges of a shared machine) / Low (trusted-caller misuse)
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: not excluded. Trigger is documented API use, then destroy without crash and sync, so O2 guarantees the directory; step 1 says 'A wrong hash after documented operations, destroying the machine, and a sync is not' out of scope. Deliberate-change exclusion covers the replacement itself, not its loss on persist. 2 Role: syncing/loading = Honest operator; replace_memory_range = rest of API, off path unless a node does it (AUDIT row 2: give both). 3 Medium case: 'A machine API operation off the honest operator's path that, used as documented, leaves ... a stored directory inconsistent with the machine's contents (R9)'. 4 Critical if on path: R2 'Every way of copying, persisting, restoring, or sharing a machine' must agree; section 4 'a directory that O2 guarantees but that later loads as a different state'. 5 Low if replacing ranges of a shared machine is misuse (nothing in cm.h says so; API does not refuse).
items.reason: Code facts checked (cm.h only says 'A later cm_store() uses the new backing store'). Medium case on off-path API leaving a stored directory inconsistent (R9); Critical if on path (R2, section 4 O2 clause).
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: machine::replace_memory_range (src/machine.cpp ~723-764; machine_address_ranges::replace ~656-683) swaps a range's backing store only in memory (m_c, m_ars) and does not refuse machines whose ranges are mapped shared to a stored directory D, nor rewrite D/config.json. After the caller loads D with SHARING_ALL (clear_hash_tree), replaces .ram, runs, destroys the machine and calls sync_stored(D), D meets O2's definition of a guaranteed directory but reloads to a state no execution reaches: post-run registers/buffers with the pre-replacement RAM. verify_hash_tree and an O1 rebuild both pass. CLI also allows --load=D,sharing:all,sync with --replace-memory-range (cartesi-machine.lua 2944-2956, 4926-4938). Required behavior: section 8 step 1 'A wrong hash after documented operations, destroying the machine, and a sync is not' excused; Medium case 'A machine API operation off the honest operator's path that, used as documented, leaves ... a stored directory inconsistent with the machine's contents (R9)'; R2 'Every way of copying, persisting, restoring, or sharing a machine' must agree. Test idea: clone bugs/harness baremetal-template to temp D, sync, load with SHARING_ALL + clear_hash_tree, replace .ram with an image differing in one byte at 0x80100000, deliver one advance input, run to yield, record H=get_root_hash; destroy; sync_stored(D); reload D with clear_hash_tree. Exit 0 if replace_memory_range raised (refusal is a valid fix) or reloaded root == H; else exit 1. Hunter evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r3/VARCACHE/replace_shared2.lua (reloaded root 0xa159... matches none of the machine's roots), replace_shared.lua. Rate both readings: Medium (off-path) / Critical (if a node does this).

items.title: Exception inside hash_tree::update after page hashes are stored skips m_bubble_up_unchanged_pages, so ancestors stay stale for good; wrong roots, proofs, snapshots; verify_hash_tree passes
items.component: Emulator core: hash tree (src/hash-tree.cpp update 758-771, update_dense_trees 503-511, update_words, update_sparse_tree)
items.role: Honest operator (hash tree)
items.severity: Critical (preferred, same reading as confirmed R1-O2-3: host fault turned into a wrong hash, R9 failed update) / Low (if allocation failure is not a covered host fault or continuing after an error is misuse)
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: host-fault exclusion holds only 'as long as the emulator does not turn them into a wrong hash'; it does. 2 Role: hash tree = Honest operator (AUDIT row 1; section 3). 3 No High/Medium case: the failing calls (get_root_hash, collectors, log producers) are on the path. 4 Critical: R9 'It includes interrupted or failed updates' with '"Interrupted or failed updates" means updates that fail inside a running process, which then keeps using the machine'. 5 Alternative Low as for R1-O2-3.
items.reason: Code checked: m_bubble_up_unchanged_pages = !update_succeeded runs only on return (hash-tree.cpp 768-769), though hash-tree.hpp 252-255 says it exists for failed updates. R9 failed-update clause, distinct site and fix from R1-O2-3.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: hash_tree::update (src/hash-tree.cpp 758-771) runs update_dirty_pages (stores new page hashes into dense trees, returns cache entries), then update_dense_trees (reserves a pmr batch of min(concurrency<<10,16384) entries, an upstream allocation on every update with a dirty range, 503-511), then update_sparse_tree. m_bubble_up_unchanged_pages = !update_succeeded is assigned only when these return; an exception (std::bad_alloc) skips it, leaving the flag false. The next update sees those pages' hashes as unchanged, marks them clean (return_updated_dirty_pages 384-394) and never recomputes their ancestors. The root stays stale until clear_hash_tree; verify_hash_tree() (661-735) only compares pages with dht page nodes and returns true. update_words and update_sparse_tree have analogous windows (read only). Required: R9 'The content hash must equal the root of the actual contents ... It includes interrupted or failed updates' and '"Interrupted or failed updates" means updates that fail inside a running process, which then keeps using the machine'; section 4 'the emulator must never turn [a host fault] into a wrong hash'. Test idea (like bugs/R1-O2-3): LD_PRELOAD operator-new replacement that throws std::bad_alloc for the request of exactly FAIL_EXACT bytes while an arm file exists; 64 MiB RAM machine with runtime concurrency.update_hash_tree=4 (batch = 65536 bytes); get_root_hash; write_memory to 64 distinct pages; arm; pcall(get_root_hash) must fail (else exit 2); disarm; one more write_memory; require get_root_hash() == root after clear_hash_tree() (exit 1 if not). Hunter evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r3/VARDIRTY/c1-test.sh, c1-check.lua, inj.cpp (cached 0x14b9... vs rebuilt 0xb664..., verify true), probe2.lua (store/load keeps stale root), nth.cpp/sweep.sh (same at collect_mcycle_root_hashes N=179/182, log_reset_uarch). Rate both readings like R1-O2-3.

items.title: Log producers not atomic under an exception: failed log_step_uarch / log_send_cmio_response leave a half-applied transition; retry on the same machine logs a non-canonical trajectory
items.component: Log producers: uarch_record_state_access log_write_access (162-185), record_send_cmio_state_access (194-250), machine::log_step_uarch / log_send_cmio_response
items.role: Honest operator (log producers)
items.severity: Critical (if continued use of a machine after a failed call is documented use, as R9's failed-update definition and R1-O2-3 imply) / Low (hunter's preference: loud failure, hash consistent with contents, retry is misuse)
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: host-fault exclusion applies only if no wrong hash results; the machine's root after the error is the hash of a state no transition produces, and a retry logs it. 2 Role: log producers = Honest operator. 3 No High/Medium case (reachable state, on path). 4 Critical reading: R4 'No reachable state makes a log producer fail' plus section 4 host-fault clause; R9's failed-update definition shows the model expects a machine to stay usable after a failed call; O2's 'combination that no execution reaches' covers only stops. 5 Low reading: error is reported, tree consistent with contents; continuing after an error may be misuse.
items.reason: Unsure between readings; Critical reading follows R1-O2-3's accepted R9/section 4 reasoning; distinct site and fix (atomic logging) from R1-O2-3 and R3-VARDIRTY-1.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: logged transitions are applied access by access while the log is built with heap allocations between writes (src/uarch-record-state-access.hpp log_write_access 162-185: write, then log_written_hash/data/push_access allocate; src/record-send-cmio-state-access.hpp log_write_memory_with_padding 194-250; send-cmio-response.cpp writes imcyclemax, revert root hash, rx data, fromhost, iflags.Y separately; machine.cpp log_step_uarch 2193-2216 and log_send_cmio_response 2107-2131 verify after the change). A std::bad_alloc between writes leaves the machine half-transitioned: log_step_uarch leaves uarch_pc advanced with uarch_cycle unchanged; log_send_cmio_response leaves imcyclemax (then revert root hash, rx buffer, fromhost) written with iflags.Y still 1. Errors after the last write report failure though the transition completed. A retry on the same machine then logs a different trajectory or a delivery whose before-hash is non-canonical. Required: section 4 'the emulator must never turn [a host fault] into a wrong hash, a wrong proof'; R9 '"Interrupted or failed updates" means updates that fail inside a running process, which then keeps using the machine'; R4 'No reachable state makes a log producer fail'. Test idea: N-th-allocation injector (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r3/VARDIRTY/nth.cpp); for each N up to the call's allocation count, on fresh machines pcall(log_step_uarch) (bare-metal guest at mcycle 1,000,000) and pcall(log_send_cmio_response) (bugs/harness valid-template, 60,000-byte payload, LARGE_DATA); after a failure require root == before-hash, or root == control after-hash with the call not failing; exit 1 on any third value. Hunter evidence: logstep.lua (N=25..28: cycle 0, pc 0x600004, retry diverges), logsend.lua (N=18..48 partial states). Decide the reading: is retrying/continuing on a machine after a failed log call documented use? Note the PRT player logs on disposable forks.

items.title: HTIF getchar reproducibility guard runs only at create/load: after write_reg(htif_iconsole) native run diverges from uarch/collectors, host console input reaches hashed state, store writes an unloadable directory
items.component: Emulator core: machine::init_console (~351-358), write_reg htif_iconsole (~1468), set_runtime_config (~415-424), full-shadow write_memory; native vs non-interactive state accesses
items.role: write_reg/set_runtime_config: rest of the machine API (off path); diverging paths (native, uarch, collect_mcycle_root_hashes, store/load): Honest operator
items.severity: Medium (preferred, as confirmed R1-R2-1) / High (divergence between paths only at states unreachable from a valid template) / Low or Out of scope (misuse / deliberate-change readings)
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: deliberate-change exclusion covers the register write, not host input entering a reproducible machine on one path or store writing a directory its load refuses (R1-R2-1 reading). 2 Role: triggering calls off path; diverging components Honest operator. 3 Medium: 'A machine API operation off the honest operator's path that, used as documented, leaves ... a stored directory inconsistent with the machine's contents (R9)'; also R14 'rules out host devices, any other host input', R1 runtime option changes a transition, R2 single source of truth. High alternative: 'A divergence between paths only at demonstrably unreachable states' (no instruction or delivery writes iconsole). 5 Low/OOS under misuse readings.
items.reason: Same pattern as confirmed R1-R2-1 at a different register and guard (different fix: check iconsole and console input in write_reg/set_runtime_config/write_memory). Medium case on off-path API (R9), R14, R2.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: machine::init_console (src/machine.cpp ~351-358) is the only check that refuses HTIF getchar (hashed htif_iconsole bit) or a non-null console input source on a reproducible machine, and it runs only at create/load. write_reg('htif_iconsole', v|1<<HTIF_CONSOLE_CMD_GETCHAR) (~1468), the full-shadow write_memory path (validate_processor_shadow checks iunrep only) and set_runtime_config({console={input_source=...}}) (~415-424) are accepted afterwards. Then a GETCHAR tohost write gives fromhost DATA = c+1 natively (5 = EOT for from_null; host bytes for from_buffer) but 0 in the uarch, collect_mcycle_root_hashes, bundles and log producers (device-state-access.hpp do_getchar). store succeeds (checks only the config copy) and its load refuses ('TTY stdin is only supported in unreproducible machines'). Required: R2 'Every register and every configuration value that affects a transition has one source of truth in the hashed state, and every path reads it from there' and native/uarch/collectors must agree; R14 'In a reproducible machine, the host reaches the state only through deliveries and deliberate changes through the machine API. That rules out host devices, any other host input'; Medium case 'A machine API operation off the honest operator's path that, used as documented, leaves ... a stored directory inconsistent with the machine's contents (R9)'. Test idea: 7-instruction guest (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r3/VARSHADOW/getchar.bin: tohost <- console GETCHAR, a0 <- fromhost, halt); reproducible machine; try write_reg('htif_iconsole', iconsole|1) and set_runtime_config with input_source from_buffer. Exit 0 if both refused, or if accepted and (a) native run, run_uarch+reset_uarch and collect_mcycle_root_hashes reach the same root at the halt, (b) write_console_input does not reach fromhost, (c) store refuses or reloads with the same root; else exit 1. Evidence: exp1.lua (native fromhost ...05 vs uarch/collect ...00; load refusal), exp2.lua (from_buffer 'A' -> DATA 0x42).

items.title: Emulator build and Docker image reuse stale untracked generated uarch files, so uarch image and pristine hash (and on-chain constants generated from that image) can come from older sources than the interpreter and MARCHID
items.component: Build: src/Makefile 668-675 (generate-uarch-pristine runs only if uarch-pristine-hash.c is absent), .dockerignore (sends uarch-pristine-*.c and uarch-ram.bin), Dockerfile 63-69; machine-solidity-step generate_EmulatorConstants.sh 21-31
items.role: Referee verifier (generated on-chain constants) and Honest operator (embedded uarch program)
items.severity: High (reading: R13 'reproducibly buildable' covers the documented incremental/image build paths, whose output depends on untracked files) / Low (reading: a clean checkout, as CI uses, rebuilds reproducibly) / Critical only if a stale build is deployed
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: no exclusion (build from the project's own Makefiles; the A1-A8 exclusion's exception applies because the emulator's build makes A6 fail silently). 2 Role: on-chain constants = Referee verifier (AUDIT row); uarch program = Honest operator. 3 High: 'A uarch program or verifier code fixed on-chain that cannot be reproducibly rebuilt, while what is deployed matches its audited source' if build-history dependence counts as non-reproducible; R13 'must be reproducibly buildable from audited source'. 4 Critical only if a stale build is used (R2 native vs uarch at reachable states). 5 Low if only clean-checkout builds count (R1-R1-1 showed clean rebuilds match).
items.reason: Facts checked: src/Makefile ifeq(wildcard uarch-pristine-hash.c) skips the uarch build; .dockerignore does not exclude the generated .c files. Unsure whether R13 covers incremental builds; keep with both ratings.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: the uarch program is generated from interpret.cpp etc. into uarch/uarch-ram.bin, embedded as untracked uarch/uarch-pristine-ram.c and uarch-pristine-hash.c. src/Makefile 668-675: '../uarch/uarch-pristine-ram.c ../uarch/uarch-pristine-hash.c: generate-uarch-pristine' and generate-uarch-pristine invokes the uarch build only 'ifeq (,$(wildcard ../uarch/uarch-pristine-hash.c))'; the top-level make builds only src. So after a checkout/pull or interpreter edit in a tree built before, make recompiles the native interpreter and regenerates cm-version.h (MARCHID) but links the old uarch image and pristine hash, with no error (the embedded hash matches the embedded image, so is-pristine checks pass). .dockerignore excludes **/*.bin except uarch/uarch-ram.bin and does not exclude uarch-pristine-*.c, so the Dockerfile's 'COPY . . ; make' reuses them and install-uarch ships the stale bin; machine-solidity-step's generate-constants builds that image from EMULATOR_DIR and takes UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH and CM_MARCHID from it while UArchStep.sol comes from the tree's uarch-step.cpp. Required: R13 'The uarch program, its pristine hash, and the verifier code that a deployment fixes on-chain must be reproducibly buildable from audited source'; A6; High case 'A uarch program or verifier code fixed on-chain that cannot be reproducibly rebuilt'. Test idea (no docker needed): git archive HEAD src uarch tools Makefile into a temp dir; write sentinel uarch/uarch-pristine-hash.c and -ram.c dated 2020-01-01; 'make -n -C src libcartesi.a' must rebuild the uarch (mentions 'make -C .. uarch', 'uarch-with-toolchain' or 'uarch-ram.elf') or refuse; part 2: the repository .dockerignore must exclude uarch/uarch-pristine-*.c and uarch/uarch-ram.bin (Python matcher /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r3/VARGEN/scripts/dockerignore.py). Exit 1 today. Rate High vs Low on whether incremental/image builds count for 'reproducibly buildable'.

items.title: Referee model accepts the unauthenticated phase-closer role from any connection: anyone can close claim admission (honest claim shut out, fabricated claim settles) or stop the referee
items.component: PRT referee model: doc/recipes/game-transport.lua (announce 530-544, announce_phase_closer 501-526, deliver 473-497, close_phase 386-398, server:run 1182-1213) with prt.lua new_referee/open_mcycle_tournament
items.role: Referee model
items.severity: Critical (preferred by hunter: close effect rated as a deployed referee deciding which claims exist) / Medium (stop effect, or whole defect read as a support stall: A8/A5) / Low (phase closer read as trusted orchestration, game-transport.lua:326)
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: not a machine API call; A1-A8 exclusion has the referee-model exception. 2 Role: Referee model; section 3 'A defect in what it accepts or derives is rated as if a deployed referee had it' (close effect derives the claim set); 'only crashes or stalls the model, even when that stops other matches (A8), is rated as support' (stop effect). 3 Stop effect: support Medium (stood-in A8/A5 Critical). 4 Close effect: Critical, section 1 goal fails; A7 'No rule of the referee may make the honest claim lose by timeout while it acts within its own clock'; manual 10608 'opens to every player subscribed'. 5 Low if the closer is trusted orchestration: manual 11308 'The referee is one trusted process' and 'gathers a tournament's claims first' are listed simplifications (non-normative per section 5), and the transport comment calls the closer trusted.
items.reason: Code comment confirmed ('The phase closer is trusted orchestration. Its announced role is not authenticated.'); manual never mentions it. Readings range Critical/Medium/Low on whether its message is an untrusted transaction; keep.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: in the PRT referee model, claim admission is a wall-clock phase that ends when the 'phase closer' answers close_phase; accept_subscribers subscribes only the connections present then (close_phase sets phase.players = get_players(), game-transport.lua 386-398), and only they receive commit_mcycle_claim (prt.lua open_mcycle_tournament 730-765). Any TCP client that first sends {"role":"phase_closer"} becomes the closer (announce/announce_phase_closer 501-544; the real closer is then refused) and its 'done' closes admission; {"role":"phase_closer","command":"stop"} at any time sets self.stopping and server:run closes the referee (1182-1213) even mid-match or during wait_for_outputs. game-transport.lua:326 says 'The phase closer is trusted orchestration. Its announced role is not authenticated.' The manual (doc/README.md ~10608) says 'The mcycle tournament opens to every player subscribed to the epoch's initial state hash'; its simplifications list (~11308) says the referee is one trusted process and gathers claims first, but never mentions the closer; ~9406 says wire messages represent blockchain events and transactions. Required: section 3 'A defect in what it accepts or derives is rated as if a deployed referee had it'; goal of section 1; A7 'No rule of the referee may make the honest claim lose by timeout while it acts within its own clock'; for the stop effect A8 and A5 'No party can make it stop accepting them' (support Medium per section 3). Test idea: start prt.lua referee with the baremetal-template hash and one input; connect prt-dishonest.lua quitter; a raw socket sends {"role":"phase_closer"} then {"value":"done"}; connect prt.lua honest; require that the honest claim is posted and wins (exit 1 if the quitter's claim wins). Second assertion: a raw socket sending the stop command while a match is open must not end the referee. Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r3/VARREFMODEL/e2e-spoof.sh (winner = quitter's fabricated claim 0x1a22...), run-exp.sh spoof_stop, probe.lua. Reviewer must decide whether the closer's message is an untrusted party's transaction.

items.title: Referee model process crashes on any connection that closes or errors without a 'done' reply, so one socket close stops every match and output acceptance
items.component: PRT referee model: doc/recipes/game-transport.lua reader coroutine assert (567), writer assert (557), accept assert (616), dispatcher step (121-142)
items.role: Referee model (crash/stall rated as support per section 3)
items.severity: Medium (support rating of a referee-model crash that would violate A8/A5 for a deployed referee) / Low (if unannounced EOF is read as a transport bug the model may treat as fatal)
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: not a machine API call; referee-model exception to A1-A8 exclusion. 2 Role: Referee model; 'only crashes or stalls the model, even when that stops other matches (A8), is rated as support'. 3 Support: 'Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for'; a deployed referee halting on any peer disconnect violates A8 'Failing to process one match's data, for any reason, must not stop, delay or decide any other match' and A5 'No party can make it stop accepting them': Critical, so Medium. 5 Low reading per the transport's run_client comment.
items.reason: Distinct mechanism and fix from R1-A8-3 (crash on connection loss vs barrier wait). Section 3 support rule gives Medium, as for R1-A8-3.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: every accepted connection of the referee server gets a reader coroutine that asserts receive_line returned a line (doc/recipes/game-transport.lua 567: 'unexpected connection loss'); a writer assert (557) and assert(listener:accept()) (616) behave alike; dispatcher step (121-142) rethrows coroutine errors and server:run does not catch them, so the referee exits. Any client that connects and closes without announcing anything, or a claimant whose process dies (including a restarting honest player), kills the referee mid-tournament or during output acceptance. Not the R1-A8-3 barrier stall. Required: section 3 'only crashes or stalls the model, even when that stops other matches (A8), is rated as support'; support is 'Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for'; A8 'Failing to process one match's data, for any reason, must not stop, delay or decide any other match'; A5 'No party can make it stop accepting them'. Test idea: run the R1-A8-3 control tournament (bugs/R1-A8-3) with the baremetal-template hash; during it, open and immediately close a raw TCP connection to the referee port (second case: SIGKILL one quitter after it posted its claim); require the referee to stay alive and the honest claim's match to settle as in the control; exit 1 if the referee exits. Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r3/VARREFMODEL/run-exp.sh abrupt (exit 1, 'game-transport.lua:567: unexpected connection loss: closed').

items.title: PRT journal cannot re-price a pending honest move once its priority fee reached --max-priority-fee: fees() rejects the bumped priority, freezing its max fee while --max-fee has room

items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: arguably not; trigger is chain activity granted by section 7 ('Raise activity on the chain that does not belong to the application'). 2 Role: Support. 3 Support Medium if stood-in High/Critical. 4 Stood-in: R4 'submits its transactions within the dispute clocks'; the operator stops re-pricing within its own --max-fee budget and its deadline move can miss the clock. 5 Low reading: the goal assumes 'the chain includes its transactions within the dispute clocks' and section 7 excludes censoring beyond the clocks; the cap is the operator's own configuration.
items.reason: Code checked: fees() returns nil when the 15% bumped priority exceeds max_priority_fee even if max fee would fit; submit then returns blocked='fee_ceiling' while the node holds the candidate. Medium/Low on the chain-assumption reading.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: prt-transactions.lua methods:fees (140-154) signs the first candidate with priority = min(max(suggested, min), max_priority) and max fee = min(2*base+priority, max_fee); for a replacement it requires priority >= ceil(prev.priority*1.15) and returns nil if that exceeds max_priority_fee, even when the needed max fee is far below max_fee. submit (192-211) then only outbids a candidate the node no longer holds; otherwise returns {blocked='fee_ceiling'}. With defaults (bump 15%, max priority 10 gwei, max fee 100 gwei), a candidate at the priority cap (immediately when eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas >= 10 gwei, or after ~17 bumps) is frozen at its signing-time max fee; if the base fee rises above it, the honest move cannot be included or replaced, and the nonce blocks all later moves. Required: R4 'The honest operator observes the chain and submits its transactions within the dispute clocks'; section 7 'Raise activity on the chain that does not belong to the application'; section 3 support Medium if stood-in Critical. Test idea: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r3/VARSCHED/test-fees.lua drives the real journal over a mock chain: submit at base 10 gwei with suggested tip 10 gwei (signed max fee 30 gwei, priority 10 gwei), advance bump_blocks blocks with base 40 gwei and the nonce unmined; assert submit publishes a replacement whose max fee covers base+priority. Today 'fee_ceiling' (exit 1). Reviewer must decide whether fee-market non-inclusion within the operator's configured budget is covered by the goal's chain assumption.

items.title: Manual's PMA istart bit layout (R/W/X/IR/IW positions, an E bit, 4-bit DID at 11-8) does not match the encoding the emulator writes into the guest-readable PMA array
items.component: Machine address ranges / interpreter state layout (src/pmas-constants.hpp PMA_ISTART_shifts) vs doc/README.md 'PMAs' (~7913-7937)
items.role: Honest operator (state layout read by guest and uarch); other side is the manual
items.severity: Medium (preferred: undocumented deterministic deviation consistent across paths, as confirmed R2-DFGUESTSTATE-1) / Critical (literal R7: memory permissions area) / Low (manual table read as informal, or no correct guest relies on the array)
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: none (guest reads documented state). 2 Role: Honest operator. 3 Section 8: 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point ... takes the severity it would have if the manual were right'; then Medium 'An undocumented deterministic deviation, consistent across all paths, in behavior that no correct guest relies on for isolation or data integrity (R7)'; R13 'The state layout'. 4 Critical under literal R7 ('Address translation and memory permissions', 'any deviation'). 5 Low if the table is non-normative (Linux uses the DTB).
items.reason: Checked: manual table bits 11-8 DID, 7 IW ... 3 R, 2 E, 1 IO, 0 M; code M=0, IO=1, R=2, W=3, X=4, IR=5, IW=6, DID=7 (5 bits), no E. Same reading family as R2-DFGUESTSTATE-1.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: doc/README.md 'PMAs' (~7913-7915) documents the first PMA word as start(63-12) DID(11-8) IW(7) IR(6) X(5) W(4) R(3) E(2) IO(1) M(0), M/IO/E mutually exclusive, readable by the guest, and the way the interpreter discovers ranges. src/pmas-constants.hpp (33-55) packs M=0, IO=1, R=2, W=3, X=4, IR=5, IW=6, DID=7..11 (mask 31<<7), no E bit. Decoded per the manual, RAM (0x...0fd) has M=1 and E=1 with DID 0; the read-only flash drive reads as not readable, executable; the rx buffer (0x3e5) as not readable, executable, DID 3. A guest M-mode load from 0x10000 returns 0x800000fd natively and in the uarch. (The manual's claim that the shadow is visible/discoverable is a manual-only error: code faults, as R8 requires.) Required: section 8 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point is a defect in one of the two. It takes the severity it would have if the manual were right'; R7 'implements ... the devices as the manual documents them, departing only where the manual documents a deviation' (area 'Address translation and memory permissions'); R13 'The state layout'. Test idea: 1 MiB machine plus a read-only flash drive; M-mode guest (or read_word) loads each PMA istart; decode with the manual's table; assert RAM M=1, E=0, R=W=X=1, DID=PMA_MEMORY_DID (1); rx buffer R=1, W=0, X=0, DID=7; no entry with M or IO together with E. Exit 1 today; passes if code or manual table are made to agree (a manual fix must parse to PMA_ISTART_* shifts). Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r3/VARSPEC/pma.lua, pma2.lua, shadow.lua. Rate Medium/Critical/Low as R2-DFGUESTSTATE-1.

items.title: Machine creation accepts flash drives and NVRAMs placed where the manual says they must not be (below RAM, unaligned to 2 MiB, past RAM+64TiB)
items.component: Machine creation: machine-address-ranges.cpp push_back_flash_drives/push_back_nvrams, machine-config.cpp adjust_starts
items.role: Honest operator (creation)
items.severity: Low
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: largely a trusted creator's configuration choice. 2 Role: Honest operator. 3 No High/Medium case: the manual states the constraints as Linux requirements, not a security-relevant point; transitions, logs and proofs work on such machines, so R4's configuration clause holds. 4 No rule violated. 5 Low ('a failure that needs misuse of an API by its trusted caller'); a resulting Linux stall is the application's (out of scope).
items.reason: Placement limits are Linux mapping requirements, not a security-relevant manual point; no transition or proof is affected; trusted configuration. Low.

threat_model_gaps: Failed API calls inside a running process: R9 defines 'interrupted or failed updates' only for hash updates and O2 covers only stops; the model does not say whether a failed state-changing call (log producer) must leave the machine at the before- or after-state, or whether continuing after it is documented use (R3-VARDIRTY-2; extends the R1-O2-3 reading).

Referee-model transport: unclear whether orchestration messages of the doc/recipes transport (phase closer close/stop) are untrusted transactions (manual ~9406: wire messages represent transactions) or trusted orchestration (game-transport.lua:326); the manual's simplifications ('one trusted process', 'gathers claims first') do not mention the closer (R3-VARREFMODEL-1).

Role of the verification-game referee: section 3 defines Referee model as 'An implementation of the manual's referee model (section 5)' and AUDIT.md names only the PRT referee model, while the manual says vg.lua's referee 'stands in for contracts that Cartesi deploys'; whether it is a referee model or a support verifier decides Medium vs Low (R3-VARREFMODEL-3).

R13 'reproducibly buildable from audited source': unclear whether incremental builds and Docker images built from a working tree with untracked generated files count, or only clean checkouts; build-time guards that fail open have no class (R3-VARGEN-1, R3-VARGEN-2; extends the R1-R1-1/R1-R13-1 gap).

Fee-market inclusion: the goal assumes 'the chain includes its transactions within the dispute clocks', but section 7 lets the adversary raise unrelated chain activity; unclear whether an operator's failure to re-price within its own configured budget is excused by that assumption (R3-VARSCHED-2).

Inclusion slack: the model does not say whether clocks must let the honest claim win in windows shorter than its inclusion time plus one block, which decides Medium vs Low for one-block mis-timing by the operator (R3-VARSCHED-1; same question as R1-A8-4).

Restart time: R4 requires restarting after a stop and submitting within the clocks, but A7 does not say whether clocks are sized for restart time, so bounded post-stop delays have no clear class (R3-VARO2PLAYER-1, R3-VARO2PLAYER-2).

Unhashed template fields and cost: section 8's snapshot clause ('nothing it carries outside the hashed state may affect any transition (R1), crash the honest operator, or corrupt its memory') omits cost, so distributor-set fields such as mark_pages_dirty that survive an O1 rebuild and slow later reloads have no class (R3-VARCACHE-2; extends the R1-O1-2 gap).

Persistence after in-memory API changes: unclear whether O2's guarantee for a shared directory (destroy then sync) must also hold when an API call (replace_memory_range) changed the machine in ways the directory's config.json does not record, and whether such a call on a shared machine is 'used as documented' (R3-VARCACHE-1).

Documentation of deviations: unclear whether threat-model statements (R8 'can never change the cycle counter') or DTB compatible strings ('riscv,clint0') count as the manual documenting a deviation, and whether guest-readable state-layout tables (PMA array) are a 'security-relevant point'; the recurring Medium vs literal-R7 Critical conflict applies again (R3-VARSPEC-1, R3-VARSPEC-2, R3-VARSPEC-3; same pattern as R2-DFGUESTSTATE-1).

Creation-time modes changed later: R14 allows 'deliberate changes through the machine API' but rules out 'any other host input'; unclear whether a runtime-config console input source switched on after creation, or a write to a register the manual calls an initial value (htif_iconsole), is a deliberate change or host input (R3-VARSHADOW-1; extends R1-R2-1).

CLI output as claim material: unclear whether lines printed in the claim-series format by implied options (--final-hash, start:) count as claims of 'a tool that computes claims' (R3-VARSPEC-4; extends R1-R6-1).
